unit.title: Parts of the soul I
unit.needIt: Understanding that your mind has different parts helps you realize why you sometimes do things you regret. It helps you plan better ways to handle cravings or habits by knowing how your brain works.
unit.why: A man named Leontius saw bodies and felt a strong urge to look at them even though he knew he should turn away. He struggled with himself but eventually let his appetite win. This shows how our inner drives can sometimes overpower our better judgment.
unit.outcome: Identify the different internal forces that influence your choices and behaviors.

quiz.q: What does Medea struggle to control in the story?
quiz.why: Medea is described as being seized by a love that she tries to quench with reason.
quiz.quote: Medea, seized with fierce desire by reason, strives to quench the raging fire, but strives in vain.

quiz.q: What is the main idea of the 'rider-elephant' metaphor?
choices: The elephant is the part of us that moves us
The rider is the part of us that feels emotion
The elephant is the part of us that thinks
quiz.why: Haidt uses the elephant to represent our drives and instincts which provide the impetus for action.
quiz.quote: Hume's suggestion in the passage that we read, he says, reason is and ought to be the slave of the passions.

quiz.q: What is the 'rider' in Jonathan Haidt's metaphor?
quiz.why: Haidt uses the rider and elephant to show how we try to control our instincts.
quiz.quote: he suggests we can understand as an elephant, which we seek to control through whatever mechanisms are possible.

choices: The part of the soul that feels honor
The part of the brain that handles language
A part of the self that is sensitive to reality
quiz.why: Freud defines the ego as the part of the self that recognizes reality and regulates behavior.
quiz.quote: The one, which he calls the ego, is a part of the self that is sensitive to reality.

quiz.q: What is 'confabulation' in the brain study?
quiz.why: The subject made up a reason for his actions because his brain's language center didn't have the information.
quiz.quote: He comes up with an explanation for why it is that he has chosen as he has chosen.

quiz.q: What part of the brain is linked to self-regulation in Phineas Gage?
quiz.why: The lecture explains that Gage's damage to the prefrontal cortex caused a loss of self-regulation.
quiz.quote: it's become clear that the damage which the pole did was to an area of Gage's called the ventromedial prefrontal cortex.

quiz.q: What did the subjects do when primed with 'elderly' words?
choices: They walked more slowly to the elevator
They walked faster to the elevator
They stayed in the room longer
They asked for a bingo game
quiz.why: The study showed that unconscious priming of certain words slowed down their physical movement.
quiz.quote: But those who had been given words associated with the elderly went very slowly.

partials: We have internal drives that pull us in different directions.
Reason can sometimes be overridden by these drives.
The prefrontal cortex helps us regulate our actions.
Some parts of our brain work automatically without us knowing.
We often make up reasons to explain our unconscious actions.
crystal.key: The human soul is divided into different parts that often conflict with each other.

decoys.text: Reason is always in total control of our actions.
decoys.why: The lecture shows that appetite and emotion often overpower reason.

decoys.text: The brain works as one single unified unit.
decoys.why: The lecture describes how different parts of the brain and soul work independently.

crystal.aha: By understanding these different parts, we can see why we struggle to act on our best judgment.
